description:
Programme or Project Overview

TU Delft invites applications for a PhD position on indoor thermal natural variation for heat resilience, within the NWO-funded Nature 4 Homes programme. Conventional comfort standards assume near-uniform indoor temperatures, yet naturally ventilated homes show large spatial and temporal variation during heatwaves - variation that may actually be tolerable, or even beneficial, when managed well. The doctoral project studies how far natural indoor thermal variation can extend before health and comfort suffer, using citizen-science field data and modelling.

The position is a salaried four-year doctoral appointment under the Dutch CAO-NU collective agreement in the Faculty of Architecture and the Built Environment. The doctoral candidate will design and run measurement campaigns in occupied homes, recruit and support citizen-science participants, analyse environmental and survey data, and develop models that link envelope behaviour, occupant behaviour and comfort outcomes. The results will inform design guidance for heat-resilient housing renovation.

Candidate profile

Applicants hold a master's degree in building physics, architecture, civil engineering or a related field, with strong data-analysis skills and an interest in occupant-centred research. Experience with sensor deployments, fieldwork or statistical modelling is an advantage, and comfort with community engagement is important for the citizen-science component. Applications are submitted through TU Delft's careers portal with a CV, transcripts, references and a motivation letter.

Highlights

  • NWO Nature 4 Homes-funded PhD on indoor thermal variation
  • Citizen-science measurement campaigns in real homes
  • Comfort, health and modelling of natural variation
  • Design guidance for heat-resilient renovation
  • Salaried employment under the CAO-NU agreement
  • Occupant-centred building research at TU Delft
